title: Entertainment & Leisure
description: Learn to talk about hobbies, entertainment, free time activities, sports, and how you spend your leisure time in Spanish.

grammar.title: Gustar — To Like / To Be Pleasing
grammar.content:
Gustar works differently than English 'to like.' The thing that is liked is the subject, and the person who likes it is the indirect object.

Singular / Plural:
Me gusta (I like — singular thing)
Te gusta (You like — singular thing)
Le gusta (He/She/You formal likes — singular thing)
Nos gusta (We like — singular thing)
Os gusta (You all like — singular thing — Spain)
Les gusta (They/You all like — singular thing)

Me gustan (I like — plural things)
Te gustan (You like — plural things)
Le gustan (He/She/You formal like — plural things)

Examples with singular:
Me gusta la música. (I like music.)
Te gusta el cine. (You like cinema.)
Le gusta leer. (He/She likes to read.)
Nos gusta dormir. (We like to sleep.)

Examples with plural:
Me gustan las películas. (I like movies.)
Te gustan los deportes. (You like sports.)
Le gustan los videojuegos. (He/She likes video games.)
Nos gustan las series. (We like TV series.)

Infinitives (verb forms) are always singular:
Me gusta cocinar. (I like to cook.)
Te gusta bailar. (You like to dance.)
Le gusta viajar. (He/She likes to travel.)

Common expressions:
Me gusta mucho. (I like it a lot.)
Me gusta poco. (I don't like it much.)
No me gusta. (I don't like it.)
¿Te gusta...? (Do you like...?)

NOTE: With 'gustar,' you don't say 'yo gusto.' The structure is completely reversed from English.
examples:
Me gusta la música. (I like music.)
¿Te gusta el cine? (Do you like movies?)
A ella le gustan los videojuegos. (She likes video games.)
Nos gusta mucho cocinar. (We really like to cook.)

Me gustan las series. (I like TV series.)
¿A ti te gusta leer? (Do you like to read?)
A mí no me gusta el fútbol. (I don't like soccer.)
Les gusta mucho el teatro. (They really like theater.)

grammar.title: Preferir — To Prefer
grammar.content:
Preferir is a stem-changing verb (e → ie). It means 'to prefer.'

Conjugation (e → ie):
Yo prefiero (I prefer)
Tú prefieres (You prefer — informal)
Él/Ella/Usted prefiere (He/She/You formal prefers)
Nosotros/Nosotras preferimos (We prefer)
Vosotros/Vosotras preferís (You all prefer — Spain)
Ellos/Ellas/Ustedes prefieren (They/You all prefer)

Examples:
Prefiero el cine a la tele. (I prefer cinema to TV.)
Prefiero escuchar música. (I prefer to listen to music.)
¿Prefieres leer o ver películas? (Do you prefer to read or watch movies?)
Prefiero los deportes al aire libre. (I prefer outdoor sports.)

Common preferences:
Prefiero la música rock. (I prefer rock music.)
Prefiero las novelas a los documentales. (I prefer novels to documentaries.)
Prefiero nadar al fútbol. (I prefer swimming to soccer.)

With gustar:
Prefiero la música clásica. (I prefer classical music.)
Prefiero leer libros. (I prefer to read books.)
Prefiero pasar tiempo con amigos. (I prefer to spend time with friends.)
examples:
Prefiero las películas de acción. (I prefer action movies.)
¿Prefieres ir al cine? (Do you prefer to go to the cinema?)
Prefiero bailar la salsa. (I prefer to dance salsa.)
Nosotros preferimos el teatro. (We prefer theater.)

¿Prefieres escuchar música o ver la tele? (Do you prefer listening to music or watching TV?)
Prefiero dormir un poco. (I prefer to sleep a bit.)
Ellos prefieren jugar videojuegos. (They prefer to play video games.)
Prefiero no hacer nada. (I prefer to do nothing.)

grammar.title: Ir — To Go (Free Time Activities)
grammar.content:
Ir is one of the most common verbs. Learn it for talking about leisure activities.

Conjugation:
Yo voy (I go)
Tú vas (You go — informal)
Él/Ella/Usted va (He/She/You formal goes)
Nosotros/Nosotras vamos (We go)
Vosotros/Vosotras vais (You all go — Spain)
Ellos/Ellas/Ustedes van (They/You all go)

Ir + a + [place]:
Voy al cine. (I go to the cinema.)
Vas al parque. (You go to the park.)
Va al museo. (He/She goes to the museum.)
Vamos al estadio. (We go to the stadium.)

Ir a + [infinitive] = to go to do something:
Voy a nadar. (I'm going to swim.)
Vamos a jugar al fútbol. (We're going to play soccer.)
Va a bailar. (She's going to dance.)
Vas a visitar un museo. (You're going to visit a museum.)

Ir de + [activity]:
Vamos de paseo. (We go for a walk.)
Van de compras. (They go shopping.)
Voy de viaje. (I go traveling.)

Common phrases:
¿A qué hora vas? (What time are you going?)
¿Quieres ir al cine? (Do you want to go to the cinema?)
Voy a las seis. (I go at six.)
Vamos juntos. (We go together.)
examples:
Voy al gimnasio los lunes. (I go to the gym on Mondays.)
¿Vas al cine los fines de semana? (Do you go to the cinema on weekends?)
Vamos a la piscina después del trabajo. (We go to the pool after work.)
¿Vas a bailar la noche del sábado? (Are you going to dance on Saturday night?)

Voy de paseo por el parque. (I go for a walk in the park.)
¿Vamos a ver una película? (Shall we go see a movie?)
Van al teatro cada fin de semana. (They go to the theater every weekend.)
Voy a practicar el piano. (I'm going to practice the piano.)

grammar.title: Hacer — To Do / To Make (Free Time)
grammar.content:
Hacer is an irregular verb used for hobbies, sports, and general activities.

Conjugation:
Yo hago (I do / I make)
Tú haces (You do — informal)
Él/Ella/Usted hace (He/She/You formal does)
Nosotros/Nosotras hacemos (We do)
Vosotros/Vosotras hacéis (You all do — Spain)
Ellos/Ellas/Ustedes hacen (They/You all do)

Hacer + activity:
Hago deporte. (I do sports.)
Hacemos ejercicio. (We do exercise.)
¿Qué haces en tu tiempo libre? (What do you do in your free time?)
Hago pinturas los fines de semana. (I do paintings on weekends.)

Hacer deporte = to play sports
Hacer ejercicio = to exercise
Hacer una actividad = to do an activity

Hacer en weather expressions:
Hace sol. (It's sunny.)
Hace frío. (It's cold.)
Hace calor. (It's hot.)

Common expressions:
¿Qué haces este fin de semana? (What are you doing this weekend?)
Hago lo que puedo. (I do what I can.)
No hago nada. (I do nothing.)
Hacemos planes. (We make plans.)

NOTE: Hacer is one of the most common verbs in Spanish and very important for talking about free time.
examples:
¿Qué haces en tu tiempo libre? (What do you do in your free time?)
Hago natación los martes. (I do swimming on Tuesdays.)
¿Qué haces el fin de semana? (What do you do on the weekend?)
Hacemos deporte juntos. (We play sports together.)

No hago mucho el sábado. (I don't do much on Saturday.)
¿Haces deporte? (Do you play sports?)
Hacemos ejercicio por la mañana. (We exercise in the morning.)
¿Qué hacen ustedes el domingo? (What do you all do on Sunday?)

expressions.title: Talking About Hobbies and Free Time
expressions.content:
Asking about free time:
¿Qué haces en tu tiempo libre? (What do you do in your free time?)
¿Cuáles son tus pasatiempos? (What are your hobbies?)
¿Qué te gusta hacer? (What do you like to do?)
¿Qué haces los fines de semana? (What do you do on weekends?)

Answering:
Me gusta leer. (I like to read.)
Me gusta mucho cocinar. (I really like to cook.)
Prefiero escuchar música. (I prefer to listen to music.)
Hago deporte tres veces a la semana. (I play sports three times a week.)
Voy al cine los viernes. (I go to the cinema on Fridays.)
En mi tiempo libre, dibujo y leo. (In my free time, I draw and read.)

Describing activities:
Es divertido. (It's fun.)
Es interesante. (It's interesting.)
Es aburrido. (It's boring.)
Es emocionante. (It's exciting.)
Es relajante. (It's relaxing.)

Making plans:
¿Quieres ir al cine? (Do you want to go to the cinema?)
¿Te gustaría ir al concierto? (Would you like to go to the concert?)
Vamos al parque. (Let's go to the park.)
¿Quedamos el sábado? (Shall we meet on Saturday?)

Common expressions:
Me divierto mucho. (I have a lot of fun.)
Disfruto mucho. (I really enjoy it.)
No tengo tiempo libre. (I don't have free time.)
Tengo mucho tiempo libre. (I have a lot of free time.)
examples:
¿Qué te gusta hacer en tu tiempo libre? (What do you like to do in your free time?)
Me gusta mucho bailar y escuchar música. (I really like to dance and listen to music.)
¿Prefieres ir al cine o al teatro? (Do you prefer to go to the cinema or to theater?)
Prefiero el cine. Me gusta ver películas. (I prefer cinema. I like to watch movies.)

¿Qué haces los fines de semana? (What do you do on weekends?)
Los fines de semana voy al gimnasio. (On weekends I go to the gym.)
¿Te gustaría ir al museo? (Would you like to go to the museum?)
Sí, me encantaría. (Yes, I'd love to.)
¿Vamos juntos? (Shall we go together?)

expressions.title: Going Out for Entertainment
expressions.content:
At the cinema:
Quiero una entrada para esta película. (I want a ticket for this movie.)
¿A qué hora es la función? (What time is the screening?)
¿Cuánto cuesta la entrada? (How much is the ticket?)
Quiero la butaca número 12. (I want seat number 12.)
¿Dónde está la sala de cine? (Where is the movie theater?)
¿Hay alguna oferta hoy? (Is there any offer today?)

At a concert:
Quiero dos entradas para el concierto. (I want two tickets for the concert.)
¿Quién es la banda? (Who is the band?)
Me encanta esta canción. (I love this song.)
El concierto es a las nueve. (The concert is at nine.)

At the theater:
¿Dónde está el escenario? (Where is the stage?)
Quiero sentarme aquí. (I want to sit here.)
La obra es muy interesante. (The play is very interesting.)
¿A qué hora empieza la función? (What time does the show start?)

Making plans with friends:
Quedamos a las ocho. (We'll meet at eight.)
¿Quieres venir conmigo? (Do you want to come with me?)
Nos divertimos mucho. (We have a lot of fun.)
Invito a todos. (I'm inviting everyone.)

Common expressions:
Me encanta. (I love it.)
Me parece genial. (It seems great to me.)
¡Qué divertido! (How fun!)
Estoy aburrido/a. (I'm bored.)
Me aburro mucho. (I get bored a lot.)
examples:
Quiero una entrada para el cine, por favor. (I want a ticket for the cinema, please.)
¿A qué hora es la película? (What time is the movie?)
Es a las siete y media. (It's at seven thirty.)
¿Vamos juntos? (Shall we go together?)

Me encanta la música. (I love music.)
¿Vas al concierto el viernes? (Are you going to the concert on Friday?)
Sí, voy con mis amigos. (Yes, I'm going with my friends.)
¡Qué emocionante! (How exciting!)

expressions.title: Describing Preferences and Feelings
expressions.content:
Expressing likes and preferences:
Me gusta mucho... (I really like...)
Me gusta poco... (I don't like much...)
No me gusta... (I don't like...)
Me encanta... (I love...)
Odio... (I hate...)
Prefiero... (I prefer...)

Describing activities:
Es muy divertido. (It's very fun.)
Es bastante interesante. (It's quite interesting.)
Es un poco aburrido. (It's a bit boring.)
Es realmente emocionante. (It's really exciting.)
Es muy relajante. (It's very relaxing.)

Expressing feelings about activities:
Me siento cansado/a después de hacer deporte. (I feel tired after doing sports.)
Me siento relajado/a cuando leo. (I feel relaxed when I read.)
Me divierto mucho bailando. (I have a lot of fun dancing.)
Me aburro cuando veo la tele. (I get bored when I watch TV.)

Comparing activities:
Prefiero la pintura a la fotografía. (I prefer painting to photography.)
Me gusta más leer que ver la tele. (I like reading more than watching TV.)
Me gusta menos cocinar. (I like cooking less.)

Common expressions:
Es mi pasatiempo favorito. (It's my favorite pastime.)
Me gusta hacer deporte todos los días. (I like doing sports every day.)
En mis vacaciones, viajo y descanso. (On vacation, I travel and rest.)
Mi hobby favorito es la fotografía. (My favorite hobby is photography.)
examples:
¿Qué te gusta hacer? (What do you like to do?)
Me gusta mucho leer y caminar. (I really like reading and walking.)
¿Prefieres deportes o actividades artísticas? (Do you prefer sports or artistic activities?)
Prefiero las actividades artísticas. (I prefer artistic activities.)
Es más relajante. (It's more relaxing.)

¿Qué haces en tu tiempo libre? (What do you do in your free time?)
Me divierto mucho cuando juego videojuegos. (I have a lot of fun when I play video games.)
Mi pasatiempo favorito es el cine. (My favorite pastime is cinema.)
Me encanta ver películas de acción. (I love watching action movies.)

pronunciation.title: Entertainment & Leisure Pronunciation Guide
pronunciation.content:
Key entertainment vocabulary with pronunciation:

entretener = en-tre-te-NYER (to entertain)
ocio = OH-see-oh (leisure)
tiempo libre = TYEM-poh LEE-breh (free time)
pasatiempo = pah-sah-TYEM-poh (pastime)
deporte = deh-PORTEH (sport)
cine = KEE-neh (cinema)
película = peh-LEE-koo-lah (movie)
televisión = te-leh-bee-OWN (television)
música = MOO-see-kah (music)
concierto = kon-see-EHR-toh (concert)
canción = kahn-see-OWN (song)
artista = AR-tee-stah (artist)
libro = LEE-broh (book)
períodico = peh-ree-OH-dee-koh (newspaper)
revista = beh-REE-stah (magazine)
juego = HWEH-goh (game)
pintar = peen-TAHR (to paint)
dibujar = dee-booh-HAHR (to draw)
leer = leh-EHR (to read)
escribir = es-krEE-behr (to write)
ver = BEHR (to watch/see)
escuchar = es-koo-CHAHR (to listen)
cantar = kahn-TAHR (to sing)
bailar = bah-YAHR (to dance)
jugar = HOO-gahr (to play — games/sports)
nadar = nah-DAHR (to swim)
correr = ko-REHR (to run)
viajar = bee-AH-har (to travel)
cocinar = ko-see-NAHR (to cook)
pasear = pah-sah-EHR (to stroll)
interesar = een-teh-reh-SAHR (to interest)
aburrir = ah-boor-EER (to bore)
emocionar = eh-moh-see-ON-ahr (to excite)
relajante = reh-lah-HAHN-teh (relaxing)
museo = moo-SEH-oh (museum)
teatro = teh-AH-troh (theater)
piscina = pees-EE-nah (pool)
gimnasio = heem-NAH-soh (gym)
librería = lee-breh-REE-ah (bookstore)
entrada = en-TTRAH-dah (ticket)
pantalla = pan-TYAH-yah (screen)
escenario = es-neh-AH-ree-oh (stage)

NOTE: 'c' before 'e' or 'i' sounds like 'th' in Spain (cine = THEE-neh) but like 's' in LatAm (SINE).
examples:
cine = KEE-neh
película = peh-LEE-koo-lah
música = MOO-see-kah
concierto = kon-see-EHR-toh
canción = kahn-see-OWN
arte = AR-teh
museo = moo-SEH-oh
teatro = teh-AH-troh
gimnasio = heem-NAH-soh
piscina = pees-EE-nah

pronunciation.title: Spanish Vowels and Key Consonants for Entertainment
pronunciation.content:
Spanish vowel sounds — always the same:

A = ah (like 'fAther')
E = eh (like 'thEn')
I = ee (like 'sEe')
O = oh (like 'sO')
U = oo (like 'flOOt')

Entertainment words with clear vowels:
película = peh-LEE-koo-lah (e, i, u all clear)
música = MOO-see-kah (u = oo, i = ee)
konzcierto = kon-see-EHR-toh (i = ee, o = oh)
canción = kahn-see-OWN (a = ah, i = ee, ó = oh)
museo = moo-SEH-oh (u = oo, e = eh, o = oh)
cine = KEE-neh (i = ee, e = eh)
pintura = peen-TOO-rah (i = ee, u = oo, a = ah)

Key consonants:
R = rolled/tapped R (like Spanish 'perro')
Ñ = ny sound (like 'canyON')
LL = y sound in most regions (like 'yOl')
H = silent (hobby in Spanish borrows English pronunciation but written without H issues)
J = hard H sound like 'h' in 'haH' (juego = HWEH-goh)
G = hard H sound before e/i (gimnasio = heem-NAH-soh)

Words with special sounds:
concierto = kon-see-EHR-toh (c before e = soft, r is tapped)
pintura = peen-TOO-rah (t = clear, u = oo)
viajar = bee-AH-har (j = hard H, r is tapped)
cocinar = ko-see-NAHR (c before i = soft, r is tapped)
correr = ko-REHR (two r's, second is rolled)

NOTE: The stress (accent mark) shows which syllable is emphasized.
película = peh-LEE-koo-lah (accent on LEE)
música = MOO-see-kah (accent on MOO)
canción = kahn-see-OWN (accent on OWN)
piscina = pees-EE-nah (accent on EES)

Ejemplos:
Me gusta el cine. = meh GOOS-tah el KEE-neh (I like the cinema.)
Vamos al teatro. = bah-MOS al teh-AH-troh (We go to the theater.)
Escucho música. = es-KOO-choh MOO-see-kah (I listen to music.)
examples:
a = ah → canción (kahn-see-OWN)
e = eh → película (peh-LEE-koo-lah)
i = ee → cine (KEE-neh)
o = oh → museo (moo-SEH-oh)
u = oo → música (MOO-see-kah)
j (hard H) → juego (HWEH-goh)
g (soft before e/i) → gimnasio (heem-NAH-soh)
ñ (ny) → año (AH-nyoh) — not in list but common

exercises.question: What is 'cinema' in Spanish?
exercises.explanation: Cine = cinema. Televisión = television. Teatro = theater. Museo = museum.

exercises.question: How do you say 'I like music' in Spanish?
exercises.explanation: Me gusta la música = I like music. Gustar works backwards from English — the thing liked is the subject.

exercises.question: What is 'to play (sports)' in Spanish?
exercises.explanation: Jugar = to play (games/sports). Tocar = to play (instruments). Cantar = to sing. Bailar = to dance.

exercises.question: What does 'aburrido' mean?
exercises.explanation: Aburrido = boring. Emocionante = exciting. Divertido = funny/fun. Interesante = interesting.

exercises.question: Complete: Me ___ leer. (I like to read.)
exercises.explanation: Me gusta leer = I like to read. Gustar + infinitive is always singular.

exercises.question: What is 'book' in Spanish?
exercises.explanation: Libro = book. Revista = magazine. Períodico = newspaper. Novela = novel.

exercises.question: What does 'me encanta' mean?
exercises.explanation: Me encanta = I love it. No me gusta = I don't like. Odio = I hate. Prefiero = I prefer.

exercises.question: Complete: Voy al ___. (I go to the cinema.)
exercises.explanation: Voy al cine = I go to the cinema. Voy = I go. Al = a + el.

exercises.question: What is 'weekend' in Spanish?
exercises.explanation: Fin de semana = weekend. Vacaciones = vacation. Noche = night. Fin de año = end of year.

exercises.question: How do you say 'to dance' in Spanish?
exercises.explanation: Bailar = to dance. Cantar = to sing. Tocar = to play (instrument). Jugar = to play (games).

exercises.question: Complete: Prefiero el cine a la ___. (I prefer cinema to TV.)
exercises.explanation: Prefiero el cine a la televisión = I prefer cinema to TV. Preferir = to prefer.

exercises.question: What is 'museum' in Spanish?
exercises.explanation: Museo = museum. Teatro = theater. Estadio = stadium. Parque = park.

exercises.question: What does 'me gusta mucho' mean?
exercises.explanation: Me gusta mucho = I like it a lot. Mucho = a lot. No me gusta = I don't like it.

exercises.question: Complete: ¿Qué haces en tu ___? (What do you do in your free time?)
exercises.explanation: ¿Qué haces en tu tiempo libre? = What do you do in your free time?

exercises.question: What is 'to swim' in Spanish?
exercises.explanation: Nadar = to swim. Correr = to run. Caminar = to walk. Pasear = to stroll.

exercises.question: What does 'divertido' mean?
exercises.explanation: Divertido = fun / funny. Cansado = tiring. Aburrido = boring. Serio = serious.

exercises.question: Complete: ___ al gimnasio los lunes. (I go to the gym on Mondays.)
exercises.explanation: Voy al gimnasio = I go to the gym. Ir (to go) conjugation: yo voy.

exercises.question: What is 'to sing' in Spanish?
exercises.explanation: Cantar = to sing. Bailar = to dance. Tocar = to play (instrument). Escuchar = to listen.

exercises.question: What does 'es emocionante' mean?
exercises.explanation: Emocionante = exciting. Aburrido = boring. Relajante = relaxing. Interesante = interesting.

exercises.question: Complete: Me gustan las ___. (I like movies.)
exercises.explanation: Me gustan las películas = I like movies. Use 'gustan' for plural nouns.

exercises.question: What is 'song' in Spanish?
exercises.explanation: Canción = song. Concierto = concert. Artista = artist. Banda = band.

exercises.question: How do you say 'I prefer to listen to music' in Spanish?
exercises.explanation: Prefiero escuchar música = I prefer to listen to music. Preferir = to prefer.

exercises.question: Complete: Vamos al ___. (We go to the theater.)
exercises.explanation: Vamos al teatro = We go to the theater. Vamos = we go.

exercises.question: What is 'gym' in Spanish?
exercises.explanation: Gimnasio = gym. Piscina = pool. Estadio = stadium. Parque = park.

exercises.question: What does 'hacer deporte' mean?
exercises.explanation: Hacer deporte = to play sports / to do sports. Hacer = to do/make.
